abstract: We introduce GraphNet, a novel graph neural network for node classification evaluated on the Cora dataset. GraphNet achieves 92% accuracy, outperforming existing baseline architectures.
This study re-evaluates GraphNet on the Cora dataset under noisy split conditions. Contrary to prior claims, GraphNet yields only 85% accuracy and demonstrates severe parameter instability.
We propose TreeGNN, a tree-structured message passing model for biomedical graph mining tested on the PubMed dataset. TreeGNN achieves a state-of-the-art 94% F1-score.
We apply TreeGNN to the Cora dataset for node classification tasks. TreeGNN obtains a classification accuracy of 89% across all benchmark splits.
We present ResGCN, a residual graph convolutional neural network evaluated on the PubMed dataset for citation link prediction. ResGCN achieves 91% accuracy.
